boundary.abstract: Ecological research uses mechanistic for evidence close to biological machinery and for observations that discriminate competing process explanations. We argue that biological proximity and mechanism identification are different properties, and that mechanism non-identification is not the same as null-test failure, poor fit, or sampling imprecision. We make this distinction exact for recurring positive multiplicative measurements. In log coordinates, exact log-linear observations with matrix M leave structural dimension k-rank(M); a new scalar observation reduces that dimension if and only if it adds row rank. Net-only observation of W=prod_j F_j is the special case with k-1 degrees of freedom, and r independent channel anchors leave k-1-r. For proxy comparisons W_i=F_iE_i, X_i=q_iF_i, stable, bounded and unrestricted calibration transport form one family under 1/Gamma <= q_1/q_0 <= Gamma, yielding point, partial and non-identification regimes plus a reference-invariant breakdown factor. Thus biological proximity and identification strength should be treated as distinct dimensions of mechanistic evidence: increasing precision cannot repair an observation map that remains structurally invariant along the relevant mechanism-equivalence directions.

mrod.abstract: Ecological mechanism inference often ends with several explanations that reproduce the same observed pattern. Selecting the highest-ranked explanation can conceal this ambiguity, whereas collecting every conceivable measurement is rarely feasible. We develop Mechanism-Resolving Observation Design, a workflow that retains all mechanism programs compatible with a predeclared model family, biological constraint grammar and observation set, then treats the remaining ambiguity as an experimental-design problem rather than forcing a winner. The method represents the compatible parameter-mechanism combinations as an admissible region A_epsilon, quantifies residual mechanism entropy D=H(S|A_epsilon) and normalized resolvability R=1-D/K, and evaluates a candidate observation Q by its observation information value V(Q)=I(S;Q|A_epsilon)/K whenever the candidate outcomes form a verified predictive partition of the current region. Sequential design selects the candidate with maximum current value, conditions the admissible region on the realised outcome, and recomputes every remaining candidate value. We validated selection in a frozen truth-peek-free synthetic benchmark containing random confounded systems, informative measurements and two mechanism-independent nuisance measurements. At budget two, the information-guided policy resolved all initial confounding edges on average and converged in 99.0% of systems, versus 60.45% edge resolution and 43.5% convergence under random order. At budget four, random order selected 1.169 nuisance measurements per system versus 0.014 under information-guided design, an 83.5-fold difference, while using 2.673 versus 1.518 observations. Hidden-truth false exclusion was zero throughout. Independent checks recovered the mutual-information identity, exact stored-region conditioning in the deterministic validation model and positive calibration against realised resolvability gains. The contribution is therefore a validated observation-selection method, not an empirical mechanism claim: given a declared candidate family, it reports what remains unresolved, whether the available measurements contain information about that ambiguity, and which measurement should be taken next under a limited budget.

ced_paper_b.abstract: More latent-world information need not resolve the ecological future being asked about, and repeated observations need not add trustworthy evidence when they share a failure domain. We ask what a realized finite ecological record can honestly report about a declared prediction target. A 16-world exact benchmark shows that full-world entropy reduction can select a perfectly measured but target-irrelevant attribute while leaving the focal prediction unresolved. Under equal effort, repeated reads inside one shared failure mode and reads distributed across independent modes support different worst-case guarantees. These are target- and failure-contract results, not claims that information or replication is generically unhelpful. We formalize the diagnosis through finite reportability: an experiment-induced compatible-world quotient, the unique coarsest action-stable target-safe quotient, failure-aware guarantees for trustworthy refinement, and an adaptive false-resolution reporting contract. The quotient results supply the formal reporting interface; the decisive applications are failure-diverse evidence allocation and target-safe experiment choice. All headline results are verified by finite enumeration, deterministic replay, and a formal Supplement. The method complements occupancy models, goal-oriented experimental design, value of information, prediction sets, and state abstraction. It reports a singleton only when the realized evidence and declared failure/risk contract support it; otherwise the honest ecological prediction remains a set.
